correctness.rationale: Period-two Fourier Parseval yields two ℓ² convolution channels; their exact Poisson-summation symbols have nonzero determinant for every t and w>0. The ratio of those symbols cannot be rational in e^{iθ}, as its meromorphic continuation changes sign and positive exponential scale after 2π translation; the impossible constant coefficient proves this. Erasing finitely many complete translation columns is a finite-rank perturbation in each fiber. Any nonzero kernel would make both outputs Laurent polynomials and force the forbidden rational ratio. Injective Fredholm positive fiber operators are invertible, uniformly on compact t by operator-norm continuity. An escaping interval indicator independently proves failure for a half-line removal. Actual standalone CHECK.py passed 67 supplementary exact-fraction/numerical checks; these do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2026 Poisson source explicitly leaves the reverse semi-regular orientation unclassified. The present theorem supplies a concrete infinite, all-positive-width reverse-orientation subfamily (every finite set of absent integer translations at half-integer frequency sampling). Full relevant primary statements of Belov--Semenov (2026) and Belov--Kulikov--Lyubarskii (2021) and standard lattice criteria were compared on implications, not titles. The 2003 Gabor excess Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 are only existential regarding removal and cannot imply prescribed complete-column erasure. Semantic searches in published mathematical records identified no equivalent statement; this absence is not considered proof of novelty. Residual risk of unindexed equivalence remains.

value.rationale: Finite deletion here removes infinitely many Gabor atoms per column, so it is not the routine preservation of a frame after finitely many atoms are removed. The theorem gives a meaningful affirmative family inside the reverse Poisson semi-regular frame problem explicitly distinguished as unresolved by the 2026 source. The algebraic obstruction via nonrational transfer functions can guide further structured-erasure classifications, while the half-line failure delineates the scope. No arbitrary-window or arbitrary-irregular-set theorem is claimed.
